thread:
Maya (CEO): Thanks everyone for joining today's all-hands. Quick follow-up thread for any leadership strategy questions — feel free to drop short Qs and we'll answer live here.
Jon (Head of Growth): Thanks Maya — will the messaging shift for marketing now that we emphasize 'serving' over 'model ownership'?
Maya (CEO): Short answer: yes. We're keeping model capability messaging but leading with predictable inference economics and portability. Think: 'ship ML features reliably at scale' rather than 'we have the best model'.
Priya (VP Product): To add — docs and templates will change next sprint. We'll publish new one-liners and 30s demos that show latency/cost comparisons.
Tess (Eng Manager): How do we avoid being painted as just another cloud vendor? competitors keep bringing up infra scale.
Ethan (CTO): We lean into runtime + developer experience. Our differentiator: unified API across hosted/dedicated/private, built-in fallbacks, and quantization/runtime optimizations customers can actually use. Not raw infra scale — it's predictable inference, not raw capacity.
Aisha (Customer Success): Customers keep asking: 'why not just use big cloud hosters?' Suggested messaging: emphasize auditability, private deployment, and SLOs for latency/cost.
Maya (CEO): Exactly — call out compliance (Private), reserved performance (Dedicated), and the Optimize tooling that reduces $/token. Also show case studies: e.g., 2x cost reduction for Customer X after using Optimize.
Jon (Head of Growth): Any change in GTM focus? More enterprise motion?
Maya (CEO): PLG remains core for discovery. Enterprise/sales-assisted kicks in when usage or security needs cross thresholds. We'll keep product-led funnels but increase SE motions for Dedicated/Private.
Priya (VP Product): Roadmap question: which gets priority next quarter — more Optimize features or expanding Private deployment options?
Ethan (CTO): Short roadmap decision: compliance-first. Next quarter: Private (KMS/HSM integrations + air-gapped installer) prioritized, while Optimize gets iterative rollout (intelligent batching and new quant profiles).
Tess (Eng Manager): Any KPIs to track for the team so we all align?
Maya (CEO): We'll publish a one-page 'North Star' doc tomorrow. Early signals: conversion rate from self-serve to committed, median p95 latency for top routes, and $/10k tokens for high-volume customers.
Aisha (Customer Success): Competitor question — they're launching a managed model marketplace. Should we compete or partner?
Ethan (CTO): For now, partner where it makes sense. Our OS: we want to be the serving layer — let specialized model marketplaces integrate via our catalog. Avoid spending cycles building a marketplace unless it directly improves serving economics.
Jon (Head of Growth): International expansion — are we prioritizing EU vs APAC regions for Dedicated?
Maya (CEO): EU first for regulatory, then APAC via partners/cloud regions. We'll publish region timeline next week.
Priya (VP Product): Quick ask: can we get a canonical 2-line elevator pitch to share externally?
Maya (CEO): Draft: 'Redwood Inference lets you ship LLM features with predictable latency, cost, and compliance — the same API whether hosted, on reserved capacity, or private.' Feel free to iterate.
Tess (Eng Manager): Thanks. Small engineering ask: can leadership clarify tolerance for latency vs cost on some internal SLOs? micro-ops need explicit thresholds.
Ethan (CTO): We'll set default SLOs: p95 < 200ms for short chat routes, p95 < 700ms for long-context generation; cost targets will be per-workload and surfaced in Console. We'll share specifics in the infra playbook.
